{{2024 Summer Olympics}}
[[File:2024 Summer Olympics medal map.svg|thumb|upright=1.5|alt=Map displaying countries that won medals during 2024 Summer Olympics|World map showing the medal achievements of each country during the 2024 Summer Olympics.
<br />'''Legend:'''<br />

The [[2024 Summer Olympics]], officially known as the Games of the XXXIII Olympiad, were an international multi-sport event held in [[Paris]], France, from 26 July to 11 August 2024, with preliminary events in some sports beginning on 24 July.<ref>{{cite web |title=Where and when are the next Olympics? Paris 2024 dates, schedule, Opening Ceremony, top athletes, Team USA, competition and more |url=https://nbcolympics.com/news/where-and-when-are-next-olympics-paris-2024-dates-schedule-opening-ceremony-and-more |website=[[NBC Olympics]] |date=16 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240729052700/https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/where-and-when-are-next-olympics-paris-2024-dates-schedule-opening-ceremony-and-more |archive-date=29 July 2024 |url-status=live |access-date=2 August 2024 |language=en }}</ref> Athletes representing 206 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated in the games.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cunningham |first1=Mary |last2=Johnston |first2=Taylor |title=How many athletes compete in the Olympics, and more details by the numbers for the 2024 Paris Games |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/athletes-olympics-numbers-2024-paris-games/ |website=[[CBS News]] |access-date=2 August 2024 |date=30 July 2024 |archive-date=2 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240802013559/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/athletes-olympics-numbers-2024-paris-games/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The games featured 329 medal events across 32 [[Olympic sports|sports]] and 48 disciplines.<ref>{{cite news |title=Olympic organizers to release tens of thousands of new tickets for the Paris Games |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/2024/02/07/olympic-organizers-to-release-tens-of-thousands-of-new-tickets-for-the-paris-games/72505000007/ |access-date=2 August 2024 |work=[[USA |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Breaking at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Breaking]] ([[breakdancing]]) made its Olympic debut as an optional sport, while [[Skateboarding at the 2024 Summer Olympics|skateboarding]], [[Sport climbing at the 2024 Summer Olympics|sport climbing]], and [[Surfing at the 2024 Summer Olympics|surfing]] returned to the programme, having debuted at the [[2020 The [[United States at the 2024 Summer Olympics|United States]] led the final medal table for the fourth consecutive Summer Games, with 40 gold and 126 total medals, while [[China at the 2024 Summer Olympics|China]] finished second with 40 gold and 91 medals in total.<ref>{{cite web |title=USA top medal table after winning thrilling last gold |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/articles/c80evjzy2jlo |website=[[BBC]] |date=2024-08-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812022213/https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/articles/c80evjzy2jlo |archive-date=2024-08-12 |url-status=live |last1=Henry |first1=Matthew |language=en |access-date=13 August 2024}}</ref> The occasion marked the first time a gold medal tie among the two most successful nations has occurred in Summer Olympics history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tayier |first=Nectar |last2=Tayir |first2=Hassan |date=2024-08-12 |title=China celebrates historic Olympic gold medal tie with US after neck and neck battle |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2024/08/12/china/china-celebrates-olympics-gold-tie-us-intl-hnk/index.html |access-date=9 September 2024 |website=[[CNN]] |language=en}}</ref> Among individual participants, Chinese swimmer [[Zhang Yufei (swimmer)|Zhang Yufei]] won the most medals at the games with six (one silver, five bronze),<ref>{{cite web |title=2024 Summer Olympics - Medal Tracker |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/summer/2024/medals/_/view/athletes/sort/total |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=7 March 2025 |language=en}}</ref> while [[France at the 2024 Summer Olympics|French]] swimmer [[Léon Marchand]] had the most gold medals with four.<ref>{{cite web |title=2024 Summer Olympics - Medal Tracker |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/summer/2024/medals/_/view/athletes/sort/gold |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=7 March 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

==Medals==
{{see also|Olympic medal}}

[[Paris Organising Committee for the 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games|Paris 2024 Organizing Committee]] President Tony Estanguet unveiled the [[Olympic medal|Olympic and Paralympic medals]] for the Games in February 2024, which on the obverse featured embedded hexagon-shaped tokens of scrap iron that had been taken from the original construction of the [[Eiffel Tower]], with the Games' logo engraved into it.<ref>{{cite news |title=Paris 2024: Eiffel Tower metal in Olympics and Paralympics medals |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/68239167 |date=8 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240208115449/https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/68239167 |archive-date=8 February 2024 |url-status=live |work=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=8 February 2024}}</ref> Approximately 5,084 medals were produced by the French [[Mint (facility)|mint]] [[Monnaie de Paris]], and designed by [[Chaumet]], a luxury jewellery firm based in Paris.<ref>{{cite news |title=Paris 2024: the Olympic and Paralympic medals have been revealed |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/paris-2024-olympic-paralympic-medals-reveal-eiffel-tower |date=8 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240208104336/https://olympics.com/en/news/paris-2024-olympic-paralympic-medals-reveal-eiffel-tower |archive-date=8 February 2024 |url-status=live |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |last1=Theissen |first1=Marion |access-date=8 February 2024}}</ref>

The reverse of the medals featured [[Nike (mythology)|Nike]], the Greek goddess of victory, inside the [[Panathenaic Stadium]] which hosted the [[1896 Summer Olympics|first modern Olympics]] in 1896. The Parthenon and the Eiffel Tower could also be seen in the background on both sides of the medal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Paris Olympic and Paralympic medals will contain chunks of Eiffel Tower |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2024/feb/08/paris-olympic-and-paralympic-medals-will-contain-chunks-of-eiffel-tower |date=8 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240208110259/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2024/feb/08/paris-olympic-and-paralympic-medals-will-contain-chunks-of-eiffel-tower |archive-date=8 February 2024 |url-status=live |work=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=8 February 2024 |agency=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> Each medal weighed {{cvt|455|–|529|g|oz|0}}, had a diameter of {{cvt|85|mm|in}} and was {{cvt|9.2|mm|in}} thick.<ref>{{cite news |title=Paris 2024: First look at Olympic and Paralympic medals featuring chunks of Eiffel Tower |url=https://news.sky.com/story/paris-2024-first-look-at-olympic-and-paralympic-medals-featuring-chunks-of-eiffel-tower-13066755 |date=8 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240208133234/https://news.sky.com/story/paris-2024-first-look-at-olympic-and-paralympic-medals-featuring-chunks-of-eiffel-tower-13066755 |archive-date=8 February 2024 |url-status=live |work=[[Sky News]] |access-date=8 February 2024}}</ref> The gold medals were made with 98.8 percent silver and 1.13 percent gold, while the bronze medals were made up with copper, zinc, and tin.<ref>{{cite news |title=Paris 2024 unveils Paralympic and Olympic Games medals |url=https://www.paralympic.org/news/paris-2024-unveils-paralympic-and-olympic-games-medals |date=8 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240208110601/https://www.paralympic.org/news/paris-2024-unveils-paralympic-and-olympic-games-medals |archive-date=8 February 2024 |url-status=live |work=[[International Paralympic Committee]] |access-date=8 February 2024}}</ref>

==Medal table==
[[File:Léon Marchand, 2023 Pac-12 Championships, 400 yard individual medley preliminaries - 3 March 2023.jpg|thumb|[[France at the 2024 Summer Olympics|French]] swimmer [[Léon Marchand]] won four gold medals at the 2024 Summer Olympics, the most of any competing athlete.]]
[[File:Francisca Crovetto 2024.jpg|thumb|[[Chile at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Chilean]] sport shooter [[Francisca Crovetto]] holding the gold medal she won in the [[Shooting at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's skeet|women's skeet]], as well as a box with an official poster given to all medalists<ref>{{cite web |title=Paris 2024 Olympics: what is this award given to athletes on the podium at the same time as their medals? |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/paris-2024-olympics-award-athletes-podium-medals-poster-mascot |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |date=2024-07-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240809063627/https://olympics.com/en/news/paris-2024-olympics-award-athletes-podium-medals-poster-mascot |archive-date=9 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Burgaud |first1=Florian |access-date=2024-08-11 }}</ref>]]
[[File:Patterson, Herashchenko, Mahuchikh, Olyslagers at the 2024 Summer Olympics.png|thumb|right|[[Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's high jump|Women's high jump]] medallists from left to right: [[Iryna Herashchenko (athlete)|Iryna Herashchenko]] (Ukraine, bronze), [[Eleanor Patterson]] (Australia, bronze), [[Yaroslava Mahuchikh]] (Ukraine, gold), and [[Nicola Olyslagers]] (Australia, silver).]]

The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref name="The Independent" /><ref>{{cite web |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |website=[[Diario AS]] |date=2024-08-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us }}</ref>

Events in [[Boxing at the 2024 Summer Olympics|boxing]] result in a bronze medal being awarded to each of the two competitors who lose their semi-final matches, as opposed to fighting in a [[Third place playoff|third place tiebreaker]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Explained: Two bronze medals are awarded in the Olympics boxing competition |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/why-two-bronze-medals-boxing |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |date=1 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328143327/https://olympics.com/en/news/why-two-bronze-medals-boxing |archive-date=28 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Ansari |first1=Aarish |access-date=2 August 2024 }}</ref> Other combat sports, which include [[Judo at the 2024 Summer Olympics|judo]], [[Taekwondo at the 2024 Summer Olympics|taekwondo]], and [[Wrestling at the 2024 Summer Olympics|wrestling]], use a [[repechage system]] which also results in two bronze medals being awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Repechage in wrestling and other sports explained – the second chance |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/what-is-repechage-rules |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |date=21 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240802015913/https://olympics.com/en/news/what-is-repechage-rules |archive-date=2 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Nag |first1=Utathya |access-date=2 August 2024 }}</ref>

In the [[Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metre breaststroke|men's 100 m breaststroke]], two silver medals and no bronze medal were awarded due to a tie;<ref>{{cite news |title=Staying out of pool helped Olympians Nic Fink and Adam Peaty secure swimming medals |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/sports/olympics/staying-pool-helped-olympians-nic-fink-adam-peaty-secure-swimming-meda-rcna164021 |date=2024-07-29
